Bring a calculator, and a laptop per pair if you can. For part 2, you'll need the t table (Appendix B of the book). Part 3 uses the [course simulator](/resource/simulator-power.qmd), so there's no workbook this week.

## 1. Your questions and the key ideas

Pritha starts with your questions about Topics 7 and 8. Then she goes over the key ideas again: power and the four ways to raise it, and the one-sample t-test: why σ̂ takes the place of σ, degrees of freedom, and reading the t table. Where we write σ̂ and σ̂<sub>M</sub>, the book writes s and s<sub>M</sub>.

## 2. By hand, in pairs (about 10 minutes)

On a 20-question fractions test, sixth graders across the country average μ = 10, but nobody knows σ. A teacher gives the test to her 6 students after a new unit, and they score:

<p class="lead">12, 15, 9, 14, 13, 15</p>

These numbers are made up.

a. Find M, SS, σ̂ and σ̂<sub>M</sub>.
b. Run the four steps at α = 0.05, two tails. State H₀ and H₁, find df and the cutoffs in the t table, find t, and decide.
c. Before she gave the test, the teacher predicted that her class would score higher than 10. With a one-tailed test, what's the cutoff? Does the decision change?
d. Why does this test use t and the t table, rather than z and the unit normal table?

## 3. Power on the simulator, in pairs (about 10 minutes)

[Open the simulator with d = 0.40 and n = 20](../simulator/index.html?tab=power&d=0.4&n=20){target="_blank"}. It shows the design from class: one mean against a fixed value. The readout on the right gives the power. To set a slider exactly, click it and use the arrow keys.

a. What's the power? Out of 100 studies like this one, about how many would reject H₀?
b. Change one thing at a time, and set it back before the next. Predict first, then check: α = 0.10; a one-tailed test; n = 40; d = 0.60. Which change raised power the most?
c. With d = 0.40, find the smallest n that gives 80% power. Check it with n = (2.80 / d)².
d. Set d to 0. Why does the readout show no power now?

## 4. Your sentence (about 5 minutes)

On a slip of paper with your name, write one sentence: what does the t-test in part 2 let the teacher say about her class, and what doesn't it? Hand it to Pritha. A real attempt earns the lab's 3 points. It doesn't have to be correct.
